meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'егодня').

examples.text: Катя сегодня уезжает в другой город.
examples.trans: Katya is leaving for another city today.
Thank goodness, we dodged a bullet today!

examples.text: Давай сегодня спокойно, я тебя умоляю.
examples.trans: Let's keep it calm today, I beg you.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('scheduled').

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'верка'). Common feminine noun meaning 'inspection' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Today is a scheduled check for alcohol.

examples.trans: Please get acquainted.

examples.text: А если он откажется от алкоголя?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лушать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'listen', paired with 'послушать'.

examples.trans: Listen, drink a little olive oil.
Listen, Samson.
Yes, I'm listening.

meanings.en: to drink up, to have a drink
meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'пить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'drink', paired with 'выпивать'.

examples.trans: Oh, I've had a bit to drink now.
Drink some water.
May I drink a tiny drop of beer?

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'много'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Listen, drink a little olive oil.
I need to do a bit of work.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('olive').

examples.trans: Listen, drink a little olive oil.

examples.text: Шеф говорит, что это очень оливковый выбор.
examples.trans: The chef says that this is a very olive choice.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'butter, oil' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Listen, drink a little olive oil.
Add a piece of butter to the pan.

examples.text: Затем добавь масло и тёплые сливки.
examples.trans: Then add butter and warm cream.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Это хозяйка нашего отеля, Элеонора Андреевна.
examples.trans: This is the owner of our hotel, Eleonora Andreevna.
The hotel owner, Eleonora Andreevna.
Eleonora Andreevna is Katya's mom.

meanings.note: Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'егда').

examples.trans: I always remembered her.
Just twenty thousand.
It always helps wonderfully.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'лично'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: It always helps wonderfully.
Fifty thousand is great money too!
I know this town really well!

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'могать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'is helping', paired with 'помочь'.

examples.trans: It always helps wonderfully.
Help Lavrov.
I always help the neighbours.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'now', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You are under my roof now.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you (informal)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And did you ever think of me?

examples.text: Подожди, ты мне ничего не рассказала.
examples.trans: Wait, you did not really tell me anything.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'come on', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

related.gloss: to give (the verb it comes from)

examples.trans: Actually, he died recently.

examples.text: А я недавно большой кредит взял.
examples.trans: And I recently took out a big loan.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'blow', paired with 'подуть'.

examples.trans: They will be present at the event.

examples.text: Все деньги пойдут на спасение животных.
examples.trans: All the money will go toward saving the animals.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А что тут у вас происходит?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'at, near, with', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Please get acquainted.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

meanings.en: to happen, take place, go on
meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'исходить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'is happening', paired with 'произойти'.

examples.text: А что тут у вас происходит?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('new').

examples.text: Старый кредит отдам и новый возьму.
examples.trans: I will pay off the old loan and take a new one.

meanings.note: Prefix 'рас-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'поряжение'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'order' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is a new order from management.
This is Victoria Sergeyevna's order, chef.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'чальство'). Common neuter noun meaning 'of management' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is a new order from management.
Well, if management ordered us.
The management signed an important order.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'come on, well', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Excuse me, I need to go.

examples.text: Мне нужно срочно выйти на воздух!

examples.trans: Thank goodness, we dodged a bullet today!

examples.text: А то, что мы с вами переспали...

examples.trans: Well, if management ordered us.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'show', paired with 'показывать'.

examples.trans: Show me your hands!
Shall we show this to Anikeev?

examples.text: Ну, покажите руки. Что у вас за спиной?
examples.trans: Well, show me your hands. What is behind your back?

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('personal').

examples.trans: So this is your personal plan?

examples.text: Пусть он сообщит об этом лично.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'example' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Ты бы брал пример с сестры!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'else/more', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'верять'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to check, test, verify', paired with 'проверить'.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Very nice to meet you.

examples.trans: Please get acquainted.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пасибо'). Common neuter noun meaning 'thank you' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Thank you, here is the key card for you.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'here, there', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Of course, I will help carry the things right now.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.trans: Right now we will say goodbye, have a drink, and all will be fine.

meanings.en: to carry, deliver something to a place
meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'нести'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to carry to, take to', paired with 'относить'.

examples.text: Конечно, я сейчас помогу отнести вещи.
examples.trans: Of course, I will help carry the things right now.

examples.text: Я сам отнесу блюдо в зал.
examples.trans: I will carry the dish into the dining room myself.

examples.text: Конечно, я сейчас помогу отнести вещи.
